content.value_statement: Python projects often need framework, async, typing, and structure decisions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Python choices.
actual_capabilities: Compares FastAPI, Django, and Flask based on project needs.
Guides async versus sync decisions for Python services.
Recommends type hint and Pydantic usage for APIs and validation.
Suggests project structures for scripts, APIs, and large applications.
Covers testing, fixtures, background tasks, and error handling patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not runnable automation.
It does not inspect repositories unless the host assistant reads files separately.
It does not replace current framework documentation for version-specific details.
It focuses on Python web and service patterns more than data science workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API
use_cases.description: Select FastAPI, Django, or Flask based on requirements, team skill, and infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Review Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Check async choices, project layout, validation boundaries, and error handling before implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Python Guidance
use_cases.description: Give AI coding agents consistent Python design rules during planning and code review.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Framework
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new Python web project.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building [project type] with [team experience] and [deployment target]. Recommend a Python framework and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Decide Async or Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these operations: [database], [HTTP calls], [CPU work], [traffic]. Recommend async or sync patterns for this Python service.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate developer organizing a growing project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python project structure for [application scope]. Include modules, tests, validation models, services, and dependency boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Architecture Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Python architecture plan: [plan]. Identify weak framework choices, async risks, type gaps, testing gaps, and error handling issues.

output_examples.input: A small internal API with simple CRUD screens and an admin need.
output_examples.output: A recommendation that compares Django and FastAPI, then chooses Django because the admin interface matters most.

output_examples.input: A FastAPI service that calls external APIs and writes to PostgreSQL.
output: Use async handlers when the database driver and HTTP client are async.
Keep blocking libraries out of request paths.
Test async endpoints with pytest-asyncio and an async HTTP client.

output_examples.input: A project that has routes, database models, validation, and background jobs in one file.
output_examples.output: A refactoring plan that separates routes, services, schemas, models, tests, and background task responsibilities.

best_practices: Start with the project context before choosing a framework.
Use type hints on public APIs, return values, and shared models.
Separate routing, business logic, validation, and persistence concerns.
anti_patterns: Choosing one framework for every project without comparing requirements.
Mixing sync libraries into async request paths without isolation.
Putting business logic directly in routes, views, or controllers.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete Python applications?
faq.answer: No. It guides architecture and implementation decisions that an assistant can apply while coding.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers FastAPI, Django, Flask, Celery, ARQ, RQ, Dramatiq, Pydantic, pytest, and common async libraries.

faq.question: Can it help choose between async and sync code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when async helps and when sync code or multiprocessing is a better choice.

faq.question: Is this skill useful for existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide reviews of structure, testing, type hints, error handling, and background tasks.

faq.question: Does it run commands or install packages?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-only and lists only file reading and editing tools in its front matter.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Ask the assistant to apply the guidance while planning, reviewing, or implementing Python code.
